title: Upgrade safety grid and provider pinset for Terraform modules used by Private VPC deployments
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Produce an operationally safe, machine-readable compatibility grid and a recommended provider/module pinset for all Terraform modules used in Private (VPC) deployments. The deliverable is a JSON/YAML manifest (pinset) consumed by CI to validate plans and by the on-prem upgrade playbook to stage rolling upgrades with automatic rollback triggers.

Background: Private deployments span multiple customer VPC topologies and cloud providers. Past minor provider upgrades have caused subtle provider/provider-plugin behavior changes that led to drift in IaC plans and, in one case, a failed node replacement during an upgrade window. We need a repeatable, conservative upgrade strategy that balances security (patch updates) and reliability (predictable plan diffs).

Scope:
- Inventory of all used Terraform providers and first-party modules across private-vpc module tree (networking, peering, eks/gke/aks integration, kms, load balancers, routing).
- A "stability grid" mapping provider versions to module compatibility status (compatible / needs changes / incompatible) and to the terraform binary versions we test with.
- A pinset manifest format (pinset.json) that CI can import to run plan-validation and a provider-locking recommendation for IAAC repos.
- A gating CI job (infra/compat-matrix-check) that fetches the pinset and fails if a plan introduces unreviewed provider bumps or incompatible module constraints.
- Runbook snippets for staged upgrade (canary tenant, canary region, alert thresholds) and health-checks to validate inference runtime after infra changes (smoke generation, KV cache sanity, latency percentile checks).

Trade-offs & decisions so far:
- Strict pinning vs range pins: we will publish a conservative pinset.json for production Private deployments that pins exact provider module versions used in the last known-good runs, while recommending permissive ranges in developer sandboxes. This reduces surprise plan diffs in production but requires a defined cadence for planned pinset refreshes.
- Provider lockfile approach: we will not rely solely on Terraform's third-party provider lockfile (terraform.lock.hcl) because different CI runners have different provider download environments; instead we will maintain a central pinset manifest and a bootstrap script that reconciles the lockfile in each repo.
- Compatibility testing scope: initial matrix will prioritize providers that historically caused regressions (aws, google, kubernetes, helm, azurerm) and modules that touch networking and node lifecycle. Secondary providers will be added iteratively.

Acceptance criteria:
1) pinset.json exists in infra-private/pinsets and is referenced by infra CI across private repos.
2) infra/compat-matrix-check job runs in CI and blocks merges that would change pinned provider versions without a matching pinset update PR.
3) A documented canary rollplay with automated health checks and rollback triggers is added to the Private upgrade runbook.
4) Compatibility grid doc (human readable) published to Confluence with a table of tested versions and notes.

Artifacts & links:
- Draft pinset schema and example: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Pinset+-+Schema+(draft)
- Design doc (inventory + test plan): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Private+Pinset+Design
- CI prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-private/pull/224 (infra/compat-matrix-check job)
- Smoke test repo used for post-upgrade verification: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-smoke-tests/tree/pinset-checks

Open questions:
- Do we require the pinset to be signed/validated (artifact signing) for high-compliance customers? (Security input required)
- How frequently should pinset refreshes occur (monthly/quarterly) and who owns the cadence? Proposed: Security triage + Infra on a monthly cadence for critical providers.

Runbook excerpt (staged):
1) Create pinset refresh PR that updates pinset.json and includes test matrix outcomes.
2) Merge to main and tag as "pinset-YYYY.MM.DD". CI will create a smoke-run artifact.
3) Kick off canary upgrade using infra-ops tooling to upgrade one canary tenant + one canary region.
4) Run smoke tests and compare latency/error baselines. If error rate > 0.5% or 95th latency regresses > 25% abort and rollback.

Risk mitigations:
- keep older pinset available and allow rolling back to prior pinset tag if a provider regression occurs during upgrades.
- maintain a compatibility-staging environment that mirrors production networking surface for preflight tests.

Notes for reviewers: the proposed pinset manifests are intentionally conservative for production usage. Feedback welcome on schema fields, CI failure semantics, and whether we should extend to OS/kernel package pinning for on-prem nodes.
updates: 2025-10-15: Ticket created — initial inventory scan started. Found ~18 distinct providers across private modules.
2025-10-16: Inventory complete for core modules (networking, compute, iam). Compiled list of provider usages into draft spreadsheet and uploaded to Confluence.
2025-10-18: Prototype pinset schema submitted as a PR to infra-private (PR #224). Initial CI job infra/compat-matrix-check added to the PR pipeline to validate schema parsing.
2025-10-19: Design review with Maya Chen (sec) and Liam O'Connor (platform). Decision: require security_review_required for pinset publish. Agreed on monthly cadence for critical provider refreshes.
2025-10-20: Implemented bootstrap script to reconcile terraform.lock.hcl from central pinset. Basic end-to-end test passes in the staging environment (no plan drift observed).

2025-10-22: Assignee Diego Ramos validated canary rollback triggers against a simulated provider regression. Next: add telemetry hooks for post-upgrade regression detection and finalize Confluence doc.
Pending: Security to confirm signing requirement and legal to confirm archival retention policy for released pinsets.
